exercises.stem: 根据语境，选择最能表达“即时决定”的选项。While the group is discussing how to light a dark room, the lights suddenly go out. Tom immediately says, “Don’t worry. I ___ get a flashlight.”

choices.label: A
choices.text: will

choices.label: B
choices.text: am going to

choices.label: C
choices.text: plan to

choices.label: D
choices.text: would like to

exercises.explanation: 事情是在灯突然熄灭后才作出的决定，应用 will 表达即时决定或主动提出帮助。因此应选 will。be going to 通常表示已有安排或计划，plan to 表示计划，would like to 表示愿望。

keypoints.title: 表达喜欢与选择倾向
keypoints.body: 用于说明对人、事物或活动的喜欢、厌恶程度，或在两个及以上对象之间作出偏好选择。

keypoints.title: 用句式表达偏好
keypoints.body: 可用“like/love/enjoy doing”表达喜欢，“prefer A to B”表示更喜欢A而非B，“would rather do A than do B”表示宁愿做A而不做B。

exercises.stem: 根据语境，选择能正确表达偏好的选项。I dislike crowded shopping malls, and I enjoy history. For Saturday, I ___ visit the history museum ___ go shopping.

choices.label: A
choices.text: would rather; than

choices.label: B
choices.text: prefer; than

choices.label: C
choices.text: would rather visiting; than

choices.label: D
choices.text: prefer visiting; than

exercises.explanation: would rather do A than do B 表示“宁愿做A而不做B”，所以应填 would rather 和 than。prefer 后若接动词，通常用 prefer doing A to doing B，不能用 than。

keypoints.title: 恐惧的含义
keypoints.body: 恐惧是面对危险、陌生事物或可能发生的不利情况时产生的不安、害怕情绪，表达时可说明害怕的对象或原因。

keypoints.title: 用句式表达害怕
keypoints.body: 可用“be afraid/frightened/scared of＋名词或动名词”说明害怕的对象，用“be afraid to do”说明因害怕而不敢做某事，也可用“be afraid that从句”说明担忧的情况。

exercises.stem: 根据语境，选择正确的表达。The weather report says a typhoon may arrive tonight. Mei is worried that the flight may be cancelled. She says, “I am afraid ___ the flight may be cancelled.”

choices.label: A
choices.text: of cancelling

choices.label: B
choices.text: to cancel

choices.label: C
choices.text: that

choices.label: D
choices.text: cancelling that

exercises.explanation: be afraid that 后接从句，用来说明担忧的情况。本句后面是完整的主谓结构 the flight may be cancelled，因此应填 that。

keypoints.title: 表达积极情感与认可
keypoints.body: “高兴”指因愿望实现、事情顺利等产生愉快心情；“满意”指认为结果、表现或服务符合期待并表示认可。前者侧重情绪感受，后者侧重对对象或结果的评价。

keypoints.title: 根据语境选择表达
keypoints.body: 表达高兴可用“I’m happy/glad...”或“That’s great!”；表达满意可用“I’m pleased/satisfied with...”或“It meets my expectations.”。先判断是在说心情，还是在评价结果，再选择相应表达。

exercises.stem: Your friend asks what you think of the school library’s new reading room. It has quiet desks, good lighting, and longer opening hours. Which reply best expresses satisfaction with the room and its service?

choices.label: A
choices.text: I’m happy that the reading room is open today.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I’m satisfied with the new reading room; it meets my expectations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: That’s great! I passed my driving test.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I can’t believe the reading room is so different.

exercises.explanation: 题干要求评价阅读室及其服务是否符合期待，侧重对对象或结果的认可，因此用“I’m satisfied with...”和“It meets my expectations.”最恰当。A和C主要表达个人高兴，D主要表达惊讶。

keypoints.title: 表达遗憾与失望
keypoints.body: “遗憾”是因错过机会、发生不好的事情或结果未如愿而感到惋惜；“失望”是实际结果低于原有期待而感到不满或难过。遗憾不一定责怪他人，失望通常包含期待落空。

keypoints.title: 委婉说明负面感受
keypoints.body: 表达遗憾可用“It’s a pity...”或“I’m sorry that...”；表达失望可用“I’m disappointed with/by...”或“I expected..., but...”。说明原因时尽量具体、委婉，避免把失望直接变成无礼指责。

exercises.stem: You booked a hotel room expecting it to be quiet and clean, but it is noisy and dirty. You want to complain politely and explain that the result was below your expectations. Which sentence is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: I’m glad the room is noisy and dirty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It’s a pity that I arrived at the hotel early.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I’m disappointed with the room; I expected it to be quieter and cleaner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: That’s amazing! The room is not what I expected.

exercises.explanation: 实际房间比原有期待更差，属于期待落空，应表达失望。C用“I’m disappointed with...”明确指出失望对象，并用“I expected..., but...”的含义具体、委婉地说明原因。B表达的是遗憾，A和D与语境中的负面感受不符。

keypoints.title: 表达意外和惊奇
keypoints.body: “惊讶”指面对出乎意料的人、事、消息或结果时产生的明显心理反应，可以是惊喜，也可以是担忧、难以置信等其他情绪。惊讶的强弱取决于意外程度。

keypoints.title: 先确认再作回应
keypoints.body: 听到意外信息时，可用“Really?”“Are you serious?”确认，也可用“That’s amazing!”或“I can’t believe it!”直接表达惊讶；随后根据消息内容补充提问、祝贺或关心，避免只重复感叹。

exercises.stem: Your classmate tells you, “Our school band has just won first prize in the national competition!” You did not expect this result. Which is the best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Really? That’s amazing! How did the band prepare for the competition?

choices.label: B
choices.text: I’m disappointed with the result because I expected them to win.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It’s a pity that the band won first prize.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m satisfied with the hotel service.

exercises.explanation: 这是出乎意料的好消息，A先用“Really?”确认，再用“That’s amazing!”表达惊讶和欣喜，最后通过提问继续交流，符合得知意外信息后的自然回应。B、C表达负面情感，D与语境无关。

keypoints.title: 表达理解与支持
keypoints.body: “同情”是理解并关心他人的痛苦、困难或不幸；“安慰”是通过宽慰、鼓励和提供帮助，减轻对方的难过或焦虑。两者都应以尊重对方感受为前提。

keypoints.title: 先共情再给予帮助
keypoints.body: 可先说“I’m sorry to hear that.”或“That’s too bad.”表示理解，再用“Things will get better.”鼓励，或问“Is there anything I can do?”提供帮助。不要轻易否定对方感受、责备对方或拿困难开玩笑。

exercises.stem: 你的同学 Maya 告诉你她没有通过心仪大学的面试，显得很难过。下列哪项回应最恰当地先表达同情，再给予安慰或帮助？

choices.label: A
choices.text: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be disappointing, but things will get better. Is there anything I can do?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Don't be so sensitive. You should have prepared better.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Congratulations! You must be very excited.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I know exactly how you feel, so stop worrying.

exercises.explanation: A先用I'm sorry to hear that表达对对方遭遇的理解和同情，再用Things will get better给予鼓励，并用Is there anything I can do?主动提供帮助，符合先共情、再安慰或帮助的交际原则。B带有责备，C与情境不符，D忽视并否定了对方的感受。

keypoints.title: 表达不安与紧张
keypoints.body: “担忧与焦虑”是因可能的问题、危险或不确定结果而表达不安、害怕或紧张的情感和态度，程度可由轻到重，并可说明担忧的对象或原因。

keypoints.title: 说明原因和程度
keypoints.body: 表达时可先说明担忧的对象或原因，再说明感受和程度。英语中常用 I’m worried/concerned about...、I’m anxious about...、I’m afraid that...，也可用 What if...? 表达对假设情况的担心。

exercises.stem: 你下周要作英语演讲，因为准备时间较少而感到紧张。下列哪句话最符合“说明担忧对象或原因，并表达担忧程度”的要求？

choices.label: A
choices.text: I'm a little worried about next week's English speech because I haven't had much time to prepare.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I am worried, but I don't know what worries me.

choices.label: C
choices.text: What a wonderful speech I gave yesterday!

choices.label: D
choices.text: I must be the best speaker in class.

exercises.explanation: A用I'm a little worried表达较轻程度的担忧，用about说明担忧对象，用because说明原因，信息完整且符合语境。B没有明确担忧对象和原因，C表达赞叹，D表达的是肯定而非担忧。

keypoints.title: 说明原因和结论
keypoints.body: “表达因果与推论”是说明一个事实、行为或事件产生某种结果的原因，并根据已有信息或证据得出判断、结论的语言行为。

keypoints.title: 连接原因与结果
keypoints.body: 表达因果时，可用 because、since、as 引出原因，用 so、therefore、as a result 表示结果；表达推论时，应先依据事实，再用 may、might、must 等说明结论的可能性或确定程度。

exercises.stem: 连续暴雨后，河流水位快速上涨，天气预报显示降雨仍将持续。下列哪句话既恰当地表达了因果关系，又基于已有信息作出了程度适当的推论？

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the heavy rain has raised the river level, nearby roads may be flooded; therefore, residents should stay alert.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The river is high, so it must never rain again.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The roads may be flooded because therefore the rain is heavy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The rain continues, and the roads are flooded for no reason.

exercises.explanation: A用Because引出河流水位上涨的原因，用may be flooded表示基于事实的可能性推论，再用therefore引出合理的行动建议。B的推论与事实矛盾，C连接词使用错误，D否定了暴雨与积水之间可能存在的因果关系。

keypoints.title: 说明相同与不同
keypoints.body: “比较与对比”是依据一个或多个共同标准，说明人物、事物或情况之间的相似之处和差异之处，使信息关系更加清晰。

keypoints.title: 按标准进行比较
keypoints.body: 先确定比较对象和共同标准，再分别说明相同点与不同点。英语中可用 as...as、比较级表达差异，用 both、similarly、but、while、unlike 等连接相同或相反的信息。

exercises.stem: 学校网站要介绍“线上课程”和“面授课程”，共同标准为学习安排的灵活性和课堂互动。以下哪一项最符合“先确定共同标准，再比较异同”的英语表达？

choices.label: A
choices.text: Online classes are flexible. Face-to-face classes are in classrooms. Both are different.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both online and face-to-face classes provide learning opportunities. Online classes are generally more flexible, while face-to-face classes usually allow more immediate interaction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Online classes are more flexible than face-to-face classes, and face-to-face classes are as flexible as online classes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unlike face-to-face classes, online classes are flexible, and both of them are completely different in every way.

exercises.explanation: B先说明两类课程都能提供学习机会这一共同点，再围绕灵活性和互动性说明差异，并正确使用了both和while。A表达零散且比较标准不清；C中的more flexible与as flexible as相互矛盾；D用completely different in every way作绝对化概括，不准确。

keypoints.title: 具体呈现人物事物
keypoints.body: “描述人物与事物”是用有条理、具体而准确的语言介绍对象的外貌、特征、品质、行为、用途或状态，使听者或读者形成清晰认识。

keypoints.title: 由整体到细节
keypoints.body: 描述时可先交代对象身份或整体印象，再按外貌、性格、功能、行为等方面补充细节。英语中常用 be、have、look、seem 等结构，并选择准确的形容词和具体事例。

exercises.stem: 你要向一名交换生介绍新同学林悦。以下哪一段描述最符合“由整体到细节、使用具体准确语言”的要求？

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lin Yue is nice. She is good and interesting. Everyone likes her.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lin Yue is a new member of our science club. She has short black hair and a calm smile, and she is patient and curious. When an experiment failed last week, she checked each step and encouraged us to try again.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lin Yue has short black hair. The science club meets on Friday. Our experiment was difficult last week. I like music.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lin Yue is a person, and she has many things. She seems maybe nice, perhaps good.

exercises.explanation: B先交代林悦是科学俱乐部新成员这一整体身份，再描写外貌和性格，并用实验失败时的具体行为说明她耐心、好奇的品质，层次清楚且信息具体。A和D过于笼统、用词不准确，C内容缺乏围绕人物的连贯性。

keypoints.title: 突出关键信息
keypoints.body: 强调是说话者或作者有意突出某个词、短语或信息，使听者或读者特别注意，并准确把握表达重点。

keypoints.title: 多种方式表达强调
keypoints.body: 口语中可重读关键词、改变语调或停顿；书面语中可用really、especially、even等词，或用It is/was...that...等结构突出信息，应根据语境适度使用。

exercises.stem: 校长想明确强调“图书馆”是周末开放的地点，而不是体育馆。请使用 It is/was...that... 结构改写下面的句子：The school opened the library on weekends, not the gym.
exercises.answer: It was the library, not the gym, that the school opened on weekends.
exercises.explanation: It was...that...是强调句型，将the library置于强调位置，突出周末开放的地点；插入not the gym进一步排除体育馆，原句的含义保持不变。由于opened发生在过去，使用It was。

keypoints.title: 用具体内容说明
keypoints.body: 举例与说明是先表达观点或介绍对象，再用具体事例、特征、原因或过程补充信息，使内容更清楚、更容易理解。

keypoints.title: 先概括后具体
keypoints.body: 可先提出主要观点，再用for example、for instance、such as等引出例子；说明含义时可用that is、in other words等进行改述或补充。

exercises.stem:
Read the sentence and choose the best sentence to complete it so that the general idea is clarified with concrete examples.

The school is encouraging students to develop healthy hobbies. ______

choices.label: A
choices.text: In conclusion, hobbies are worth discussing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: For example, playing basketball can improve physical fitness, while reading biographies can broaden knowledge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: That is, the school has changed its timetable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: However, some students have little free time.

exercises.explanation: B先概括健康爱好的意义，再用“For example”引出打篮球和读人物传记两个具体事例，并说明其作用，使原观点更加清楚。A是总结，C是改述但内容不对应，D表示转折，都没有提供恰当的具体例子。

keypoints.title: 明确含义和范围
keypoints.body: 解释与定义是对事物、概念或现象的含义、特征和范围作清楚说明。定义着重回答“是什么”，解释还可说明原因、过程或作用。

keypoints.title: 先定义再解释
keypoints.body: 定义常用A is...、A means...、A refers to...等表达；解释可用because、so、that is to say等说明原因、结果或具体含义。

exercises.stem: An English club is preparing a short introduction for new members. Which sentence best defines the term and then adds an explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A growth mindset refers to the belief that abilities can develop through effort and learning. That is to say, a mistake is viewed as information that can guide further improvement, rather than proof of failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: For instance, a student may keep practising after getting a low score.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In short, everyone should try to do better.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The term is often mentioned in discussions about education.

exercises.explanation: A用“refers to”明确回答“growth mindset是什么”，随后用“That is to say”进一步说明这种观念如何看待错误，符合先定义、再解释的组织方式。B只举例，C是总结，D信息过于笼统。

keypoints.title: 提炼主要信息
keypoints.body: 归纳与总结是从若干事实、观点或细节中提取共同要点和核心内容，形成简明、完整的概括。归纳侧重提炼规律，总结侧重概括整体。

keypoints.title: 提取要点再概括
keypoints.body: 先找出反复出现的主题和关键信息，区分主要与次要内容，再合并同类信息并删去细节；可用in short、overall、in conclusion、to sum up引出概括。

exercises.stem:
Read the paragraph and choose the best overall summary.

Many students think that protecting the environment requires expensive equipment. In fact, carrying a reusable bottle reduces the use of disposable plastic; walking or cycling for short trips cuts fuel use; and turning off unused lights saves electricity. None of these actions is difficult, but together they can make daily life more sustainable.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Overall, simple everyday actions can reduce waste and energy use and support a more sustainable lifestyle.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Students should carry reusable bottles instead of using plastic ones.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Walking and cycling are the most important environmental actions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protecting the environment always requires expensive equipment.

exercises.explanation: A提取了文段反复强调的核心：日常简单行动能够减少浪费和能源消耗，并促进可持续生活，同时删去了可重复使用水瓶、步行骑车和关灯等具体细节。B只概括了一个例子，C夸大并改变了原意，D与文段观点相反。

keypoints.title: 询问并提供信息
keypoints.body: 询问与告知信息是交际双方围绕人物、时间、地点、原因、方式等内容进行提问和回答，以获取或传递事实、情况和相关细节。

keypoints.title: 问清并答全信息
keypoints.body: 询问时根据目的选择合适的疑问词，语气自然有礼；回答时紧扣问题，提供准确、完整的信息，必要时补充时间、地点或原因等细节。

exercises.stem: At the school office, you ask about a career talk. The secretary says, “It will be held next Friday, but the time and room have changed.” You ask, “Could you tell me when and where it will be held?” Which reply gives the information completely and naturally?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Certainly. It will begin at 3:00 p.m. next Friday in Room 204.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, it is about careers and very useful.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Next Friday, but I don’t know the room.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Why do you want to know?

exercises.explanation: 问题询问的是活动的时间和地点。A同时给出了具体时间“next Friday at 3:00 p.m.”和地点“Room 204”，信息完整，且语气礼貌自然。B没有回答时间和地点，C缺少具体地点，D没有提供所需信息。

keypoints.title: 提出帮助并回应
keypoints.body: 提供帮助与接受拒绝是主动表示愿意为他人提供帮助，并对对方的帮助提议作出接受或礼貌拒绝的交际行为。

keypoints.title: 礼貌提出与回应
keypoints.body: 提供帮助时先了解对方需要，再说明能做什么；接受时表达感谢并说明需要，拒绝时可说明原因、致谢，并在适当时提出替代办法。

exercises.stem: A classmate says, “You look busy preparing the exhibition. Shall I help you arrange the chairs?” Which reply is the most appropriate acceptance of the offer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, please. Could you put these chairs in two rows? Thanks a lot.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, you may not.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The exhibition is tomorrow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You should arrange them yourself.

exercises.explanation: 接受帮助时应先表达感谢，再说明需要对方做什么。A用“Yes, please”和“Thanks a lot”表示接受与感谢，并具体说明了摆放椅子的任务，符合礼貌交际原则。其余选项要么拒绝帮助，要么没有回应帮助提议，或语气不恰当。

keypoints.title: 影响选择或劝止行为
keypoints.body: 说服与劝阻是通过表达观点、说明理由和提出建议，使他人接受某种想法或采取某种行动，或停止可能不合适、有害的行为。

keypoints.title: 理由充分地劝说
keypoints.body: 先明确观点，再结合事实、后果或他人需要说明理由，提出可行建议；劝阻时指出风险并给出替代做法，保持尊重，不强迫或讽刺对方。

exercises.stem: Your friend wants to check a map on a mobile phone while cycling. Which is the most effective and polite way to persuade your friend not to do it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Don’t be stupid. You always make bad decisions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It may be unsafe because looking at your phone distracts you. Let’s pull over somewhere safe and check the map first.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Do whatever you want; I don’t care.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You must listen to me because I’m your friend.

exercises.explanation: 劝阻应明确指出风险、说明理由，并提出可行的替代做法。B说明骑车看手机会分散注意力、可能不安全，同时建议先在安全处停车查看地图，语气尊重且理由充分。A带有侮辱性，C没有劝阻作用，D以身份强迫对方接受。

keypoints.title: 提示注意并防范风险
keypoints.body: 提醒与警告都是使对方注意某件事或某种风险、避免出现问题的交际行为；提醒通常较委婉，警告语气更严肃，强调可能造成的不良后果。

keypoints.title: 语气要与风险匹配
keypoints.body: 不要把普通提醒说得过于严厉，也不要对明显危险只作轻描淡写的提示。表达时应说明需要注意的事项或潜在后果，避免含糊和无依据的恐吓。

exercises.stem: A student is about to touch a damaged power cable with exposed wires. What should you say to give an appropriate warning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: You could take a look at that cable when you have time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stay away from that damaged cable! It may still be live, and touching it could cause serious injury.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cable is over there, isn't it?

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is no need to worry; electricity is always safe.

exercises.explanation: The exposed wires indicate a serious and immediate danger, so a firm warning is appropriate. B clearly states what to avoid and explains the possible consequence. A is too mild, while C is unclear and D gives unsafe information.

keypoints.title: 概念与功能
keypoints.body: 请求是请他人做某事；许可是询问或给予做某事的允许。二者都属于交际中的礼貌表达，需要根据身份、关系和场合调整语气。

keypoints.title: 表达与应答
keypoints.body: 请求可用Could you...？、Would you mind...？；请求许可可用May I...？、Can I...？。回应时可用Sure、Of course表示同意，也可用Sorry, but...礼貌拒绝，并说明原因。

exercises.stem: You want to use your classmate's laptop to send an important file. Which exchange is the most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A: May I use your laptop for a minute to send this file?  B: Sorry, but I'm using it for an online meeting right now.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A: Could you use your laptop for me?  B: Sure, but you need to ask permission first.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A: You should let me use your laptop.  B: That's a good idea.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A: Would you mind sending this file for me?  B: May I?

exercises.explanation: “May I use...?” is a polite way to ask for permission. The reply “Sorry, but...” politely refuses and gives a reason. The other exchanges either confuse asking someone to do something with asking for permission or use an unsuitable response.

keypoints.title: 建议的含义
keypoints.body: 建议与劝告是针对某种问题或行动提出看法和做法，帮助对方作出选择。表达时通常保留对方自主决定的空间，不等同于命令。

keypoints.title: 提出与回应
keypoints.body: 可用You should...、You could...、Why don’t you...？或If I were you, I’d...提出建议。接受时可说That’s a good idea；不接受时应说明理由并礼貌回应。

exercises.stem: Your friend says, “I often forget my words during presentations.” Which reply gives suitable advice while leaving your friend room to decide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: You should prepare a few key words and rehearse aloud.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop giving presentations forever.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Could you pass me the paper?

choices.label: D
choices.text: You are forgetting words again.

exercises.explanation: A directly addresses the problem and offers practical advice using “You should...”. It helps the friend make a choice rather than issuing an extreme command. B is overly forceful, and C and D are not appropriate advice.

keypoints.title: 道歉的含义
keypoints.body: 道歉是对自己的过失、失礼或给他人造成的不便表示歉意，并承担相应责任。应答道歉则是接受对方的歉意、表示谅解，或说明问题仍需解决。

keypoints.title: 道歉与应答
keypoints.body: 可用I’m sorry for/about...、I apologize for...表达歉意，必要时说明原因并提出补救办法。对方可用That’s all right、No worries或It doesn’t matter回应；较严重的事情不宜只用轻描淡写的表达。

exercises.stem: Your teammate says, “I’m sorry for missing the deadline and causing trouble. I’ll finish the report tonight.” Which is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: That’s all right. Forget the report.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No worries. The deadline doesn’t matter anymore.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I appreciate your apology. Please send it tonight, because we still need it for tomorrow’s meeting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Never mind. You shouldn’t mention it again.

exercises.explanation: 事情已经造成影响，不能只用轻描淡写的方式表示谅解。C既接受并认可对方的道歉，又明确说明报告仍需按时完成，体现了较严重情况下道歉与应答的恰当方式。

keypoints.title: 约会与预约
keypoints.body: 约会与预约是事先协商并确定见面、活动或接受服务的时间、地点等安排。有效沟通应使双方明确目的、时间和地点，并确认彼此是否方便。

keypoints.title: 安排与变更
keypoints.body: 先说明目的，再询问时间和地点，如Are you free...？、Does...work for you？或I’d like to make an appointment...。达成一致后确认安排；需要改期或取消时应尽早说明并致歉。

exercises.stem: You need to meet the school counselor to discuss your course choices. You are free on Wednesday afternoon. Which sentence is the most appropriate for making an appointment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: I want to see you. Wednesday.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I’d like to make an appointment to discuss my course choices. Would 3 p.m. on Wednesday in your office work for you?

choices.label: C
choices.text: See you on Wednesday, maybe.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Come to your office on Wednesday afternoon.

exercises.explanation: B先说明预约目的，再提出具体时间和地点，并询问对方是否方便，信息完整且语气礼貌。A和D表达生硬，C没有确定具体安排。

keypoints.title: 告别的交际功能
keypoints.body: 告别是在交谈结束或即将离开时，用英语表达结束互动、礼貌道别以及再次联系愿望的社会交往功能。

keypoints.title: 根据场合选择表达
keypoints.body: 可用Goodbye或Bye表示再见，用See you later表示以后再见，用Take care或Have a nice day表达祝愿；回应他人道别时可说Bye或See you。

exercises.stem: You and your classmate have finished talking for the day. You hope to meet her again tomorrow. Which is the most appropriate way to say goodbye?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Take care. See you tomorrow.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I’m sorry for being late.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Does tomorrow work for you?

choices.label: D
choices.text: That’s all right.

exercises.explanation: A包含告别用语“Take care”和再次联系的表达“See you tomorrow”，符合交谈结束、即将离开并希望再次见面的语境。B用于道歉，C用于约定，D用于回应道歉或表示谅解。

keypoints.title: 问候的交际功能
keypoints.body: 问候与应答是在见面、开始交谈或特定时段时，表达关注和礼貌，并对对方问候作出合适回应的社会交往功能。

keypoints.title: 做到问候得体
keypoints.body: 正式场合可用Good morning或Hello，熟人间可用Hi；回答How are you?可说I'm fine, thanks.或Pretty good.，并用And you?反问。

exercises.stem: 早上在学校门口，你遇到校长。校长说：“Good morning. How are you?” 你最恰当的回应是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: Good morning. I'm fine, thanks. And you?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hi. This is my friend.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Would you like some tea?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nice to meet you yesterday.

exercises.explanation: 在正式场合可用“Good morning”回应问候；回答“How are you?”可说“I'm fine, thanks.”，再用“And you?”礼貌地询问对方情况，因此A最恰当。

keypoints.title: 介绍的交际功能
keypoints.body: 介绍与自我介绍是在初次交往或需要说明身份时，向他人说明自己或第三方的姓名、身份等基本信息并建立联系的社会交往功能。

keypoints.title: 按顺序介绍信息
keypoints.body: 自我介绍可按问候、姓名、身份或兴趣组织，如Hello, I'm...；介绍他人可说This is...；听者可用Nice to meet you.或Nice to meet you, too.回应。

exercises.stem: 第一次见到一位新同学时，你想进行自我介绍，并礼貌回应对方。下列对话最恰当的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: A: Hello, I'm Lily. I'm a new student.  B: Nice to meet you, Lily. I'm Tom.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A: Hello, I'm Lily.  B: I'm fine, thanks. And you?

choices.label: C
choices.text: A: Hello, I'm Lily.  B: I'm sorry, I can't.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A: This is Lily.  B: Would you like to watch a film?

exercises.explanation: 自我介绍可用“Hello, I'm...”说明姓名或身份；听到介绍后可用“Nice to meet you.”礼貌回应。A完整体现了自我介绍和初次见面的应答。

keypoints.title: 邀请的交际功能
keypoints.body: 邀请与应答是在希望他人参加活动、到某处或共同做某事时发出邀请，并对接受或拒绝作出礼貌回应的社会交往功能。

keypoints.title: 礼貌发出与回应邀请
keypoints.body: 可用Would you like to...?发出邀请；接受时说Yes, I'd love to.或That sounds great.；不能参加时先致谢，再说I'm sorry, I can't.并可说明原因。

exercises.stem: 朋友邀请你周六一起看电影：“Would you like to watch a movie with us on Saturday?” 你愿意参加，最恰当的回应是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, I'd love to. That sounds great.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I'm fine, thanks. And you?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nice to meet you, too.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I'm sorry, I can't. I have to study.

exercises.explanation: 接受邀请时可以说“Yes, I'd love to.”或“That sounds great.”。D是礼貌拒绝邀请的表达，与题目中“愿意参加”的情境不符，因此A正确。

keypoints.title: 表达感谢并回应
keypoints.body: “感谢与应答”是交际双方表达谢意并作出礼貌回应的语言行为。感谢可针对帮助、礼物或善意；应答表示接受谢意，体现礼貌与友好。

keypoints.title: 按情境礼貌回应
keypoints.body: 得到帮助或礼物时可说 Thank you. 或 Thanks.；回应感谢时可说 You’re welcome.、Not at all. 或 My pleasure.，并根据正式程度选择表达。

exercises.stem: A: Thanks for showing me how to use the new software.\nB: ______

choices.label: A
choices.text: Good luck!

choices.label: B
choices.text: Congratulations!

choices.label: C
choices.text: You're welcome.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I'm afraid not.

exercises.explanation: A 已经因对方提供帮助而表达感谢，B 应礼貌回应。You're welcome. 是回应感谢的常用表达，表示“不客气”。

keypoints.title: 区分祝愿与祝贺
keypoints.body: 祝愿是对他人未来顺利、成功或幸福的良好期望；祝贺是对已经发生或正在发生的喜事、成就表示欣喜和赞许。

keypoints.title: 选择恰当表达
keypoints.body: 活动或考试前可用 Good luck!、I hope you succeed. 表达祝愿；取得成绩或遇到喜事时可用 Congratulations on... 表达祝贺，通常用 Thank you. 回应。

exercises.stem: 你的朋友明天要参加一场重要考试，目前考试还没有开始。你最恰当的表达是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: Congratulations on passing your exam!

choices.label: B
choices.text: Good luck with your exam!

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thanks for your exam!

choices.label: D
choices.text: You're welcome for your exam!

exercises.explanation: 考试尚未开始，应该表达对未来顺利的祝愿，因此用 Good luck with your exam!。Congratulations 通常用于已经发生的成就或喜事，不能用于此处。

keypoints.title: 固定搭配关系
keypoints.body: 形容词与介词的搭配是英语中约定俗成的词语组合，介词通常由形容词决定，介词后接名词、代词或动名词，如 be good at、be interested in、be afraid of。

keypoints.title: 按词块记忆使用
keypoints.body: 学习形容词时连同介词和例句整体记忆；造句时先确定形容词，再使用常见介词，并检查介词后的成分是否正确。

keypoints.title: 避免直译替换介词
keypoints.body: 不要按照汉语习惯随意选择介词，也不要把固定搭配中的介词省略或替换。例如应说 be good at，而不能说 be good in 来表示“擅长”。

exercises.stem: Although Kevin was a beginner, he was already good ______ explaining science ideas to his classmates.

choices.label: A
choices.text: in

choices.label: B
choices.text: on

choices.label: C
choices.text: at

choices.label: D
choices.text: of

exercises.explanation: 表示“擅长做某事”使用固定搭配 be good at，介词 at 后接动名词 explaining，因此应选 C。

keypoints.title: 习语和谚语是什么
keypoints.body: 习语是约定俗成、整体意义常不能由字面直接推断的固定表达；谚语是流传广泛、形式简练且常蕴含生活经验或道理的句子。

keypoints.title: 形式固定意义整体
keypoints.body: 习语和谚语的词序、用词通常较固定，不能任意替换；理解时应关注整体意义和文化语境，而不能只按单个词逐字翻译。

keypoints.title: 结合语境理解运用
keypoints.body: 先根据上下文判断其整体含义，再确认使用场合和语气；表达时尽量保持原有结构，避免把习语或谚语用于不合适的语境。

exercises.stem: After Lina was rejected by her first-choice university, she felt that all her opportunities were gone. Her teacher told her, “When one door closes, another opens.” Which interpretation is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One should wait for a closed door to open again.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The end of one opportunity may lead to a new opportunity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every building should have at least two doors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: People should never change their original plans.

exercises.explanation: 这是一句谚语，不能按字面理解为真的有门开关。它整体表达的道理是：一个机会结束后，可能会出现新的机会。结合 Lina 被拒后仍可能寻找其他学校的语境，B 最合适。

keypoints.title: 短语动词是什么
keypoints.body: 短语动词是动词同副词小品词或介词等组成、作为一个整体使用的固定结构，整体意义有时不同于各词字面义，如 give up（放弃）、look after（照料）。

keypoints.title: 掌握短语动词用法
keypoints.body: 先把短语动词整体记忆，再确认是否及物、宾语位置和代词规则。可分开的结构如 turn off the light/turn the light off；代词通常置于动词和小品词之间：turn it off。

exercises.stem: The alarm is ringing. Please ___ before it wakes everyone.

choices.label: A
choices.text: turn off it

choices.label: B
choices.text: turn it off

choices.label: C
choices.text: turn it

choices.label: D
choices.text: off turn it

exercises.explanation: turn off 是短语动词，表示“关掉”，在本句中可分开使用。宾语是代词 it 时，代词通常必须放在动词 turn 和小品词 off 之间，因此应为 turn it off，不能说 turn off it。

keypoints.title: 动名搭配是什么
keypoints.body: 动词与名词的搭配是英语中动词与特定名词按习惯结合的词语组合，整体表达自然、常用的意义，如 make a decision、do homework、take a photo。

keypoints.title: 正确选择动词
keypoints.body: 表达时先看语境和名词，优先调用已学搭配，不按汉语逐词直译；同时检查冠词、单复数和时态。例如通常说 make a decision，不说 do a decision。

exercises.stem: Before dinner, Jack usually ___ in the study.

choices.label: A
choices.text: does his homework

choices.label: B
choices.text: makes his homework

choices.label: C
choices.text: takes his homework

choices.label: D
choices.text: gives his homework

exercises.explanation: 表示“做作业”时，英语中的固定动名搭配是 do homework。本句主语 Jack 是第三人称单数，动词用 does，因此正确表达是 does his homework，而不是按汉语习惯使用 make。

keypoints.title: 动介搭配是什么
keypoints.body: 动词与介词的搭配是动词与特定介词形成的固定或常用组合，介词后接名词、代词或动名词作宾语，如 depend on the result、look at the picture。

keypoints.title: 介词不可随意替换
keypoints.body: 介词不能只凭汉语意思选择或替换，应整体记忆搭配。例如说 depend on，不说 depend of；介词后用宾格代词，如 listen to him，不说 listen to he。

exercises.stem: 选择动词与介词搭配及介词宾语使用均正确的句子。

choices.label: A
choices.text: We depend on the weather and listen to him carefully.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We depend of the weather and listen to he carefully.

choices.label: C
choices.text: We depend on the weather and listen to he carefully.

choices.label: D
choices.text: We depend of the weather and listen him carefully.

exercises.explanation: depend 与介词 on 构成固定搭配 depend on；listen 与介词 to 构成搭配 listen to。介词 to 后应接宾格代词 him，而不能接主格代词 he。因此只有 A 正确。

keypoints.title: 反义关系是什么
keypoints.body: 反义词与对立关系指两个词在意义上相反或相对的语义关系，如 hot–cold、buy–sell。对立不一定表示绝对相反，具体含义还要结合语境判断。

keypoints.title: 三类常见对立
keypoints.body: 程度反义有中间状态，如 hot–cold；互补反义通常非此即彼，如 alive–dead；关系反义从相反角度描述同一关系，如 buy–sell。

exercises.stem: 下列关于反义词及其对立类型的说法，正确的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: hot–cold 是互补反义，因为二者通常非此即彼。

choices.label: B
choices.text: alive–dead 是程度反义，因为二者之间总有明显的中间状态。

choices.label: C
choices.text: buy–sell 是关系反义，分别从交易双方相反的角度描述同一交易关系。

choices.label: D
choices.text: tall–short 是关系反义，因为它们描述同一关系的两个方面。

exercises.explanation: buy 和 sell 分别表示交易双方的相反行为，属于关系反义。hot–cold 和 tall–short 通常属于程度反义，存在不同程度或中间状态；alive–dead 在通常用法中属于互补反义，通常不是此即彼。

keypoints.title: 褒贬色彩是什么
keypoints.body: 词的褒贬色彩是词语除基本指称意义外所带的评价态度，通常表现为褒义、贬义或中性；具体语境、说话者意图和表达方式可能使色彩发生变化。

keypoints.title: 结合语境判断
keypoints.body: 判断词语色彩时，先看其基本意义，再观察上下文、搭配、说话者态度和表达目的；不能只依据词典释义或直译判断褒贬。

exercises.stem: 阅读语境，判断画线词的褒贬色彩。After the team lost, the coach described Mei as “determined”: she kept trying after each setback. A hostile blogger called her “stubborn” because she would not consider other opinions. 关于 determined 和 stubborn 在上述语境中的色彩，正确的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: determined 褒义，stubborn 贬义。

choices.label: B
choices.text: determined 贬义，stubborn 褒义。

choices.label: C
choices.text: 两个词都只是中性词，在任何语境中褒贬色彩都不变。

choices.label: D
choices.text: 两个词在该语境中都表示贬义。

exercises.explanation: 教练用 determined 肯定 Mei 在挫折后坚持努力的品质，带有褒义；博主用 stubborn 批评她拒绝考虑他人意见，带有贬义。判断词语色彩不能只看基本释义，还要结合说话者身份、搭配和表达态度；同一个词在其他语境中可能发生色彩变化。

keypoints.title: 基本关系与语义场
keypoints.body: 上位词表示较概括的类别，下位词表示其中较具体的成员，二者构成包含关系；一组围绕共同主题或概念、意义相互关联的词，构成语义场。

keypoints.title: 关系具有层级性
keypoints.body: 上下位关系具有层级性和传递性，下位词通常继承上位词的类别意义；语义场能组织相关词汇，但场内词语不一定都构成上下位关系。

exercises.stem: In the following transport-related word set—vehicle, car, bicycle, and wheel—which analysis is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Car is a hypernym of vehicle, and bicycle is a hyponym of car.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vehicle is a hypernym of car and bicycle; car and bicycle are co-hyponyms, while wheel belongs to the same semantic field but is not their hyponym.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vehicle, car, bicycle, and wheel form a complete chain of hyponymy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Car and bicycle are synonyms because both can be used for transportation.

exercises.explanation: Vehicle表示较概括的交通工具类别，是car和bicycle的上位词；car和bicycle是同一上位词下的并列下位词。Wheel与交通有关，可以属于同一语义场，但它与vehicle之间主要是部分—整体关系，不是上下位关系。

keypoints.title: 一词多义是什么
keypoints.body: 一词多义指同一词形在不同语境中具有两个或多个相互关联的意义，这些意义常由本义引申而来；判断时要注意与意义无关的同形异义词区别。

keypoints.title: 根据语境选义
keypoints.body: 先阅读完整句子和上下文，再结合词性、常见搭配及语境确定具体义项；不要只按词典中的第一义项或单个中文译词理解。

exercises.stem:
Read the two sentences.
(1) The hikers stopped at the foot of the mountain.
(2) Write your name at the foot of the page.
Which statement is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Foot means a unit of length in both sentences.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The two uses are unrelated homonyms because neither a mountain nor a page has a body.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Foot illustrates polysemy: its basic body-part sense has extended to mean the lower or base part of something, and the context determines the specific meaning.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because foot is the same noun in both sentences, it must have exactly the same meaning.

exercises.explanation: 在第一句中，foot指山脚；在第二句中，指页面底部。两个义项都与“身体的脚位于下部”这一概念有关，属于同一词形的相关意义，而不是毫无关联的同形异义词。具体义项要结合mountain和page等语境判断。

keypoints.title: 同义词的差异
keypoints.body: 同义词是核心意义相同或相近、但在使用上存在差异的词。它们可能在语义范围、搭配、语体、感情色彩或句法功能方面不同，因此通常不能完全互换。

keypoints.title: 多角度辨析使用
keypoints.body: 辨析同义词时，先明确语境需要的意义，再比较语义范围、固定搭配、正式程度、感情色彩和句法功能，最后代入句子检验是否自然。

exercises.stem: Choose the pair that best completes the sentence.\n\nThe spokesperson ___ that the company would reduce plastic waste, but refused to ___ to reporters afterward.

choices.label: A
choices.text: said; speak

choices.label: B
choices.text: told; talk

choices.label: C
choices.text: spoke; say

choices.label: D
choices.text: said; tell

exercises.explanation: Say通常后接所说的内容或that从句，因此用said that the company would...；speak可与to someone搭配，故用speak to reporters。Tell通常需要接人作宾语，如told reporters；say不能直接用于to reporters这一结构。

keypoints.title: 基数词与序数词
keypoints.body: 数词是表示数量或顺序的词。基数词表示“多少”，如one、twenty；序数词表示“第几”，如first、twentieth，常用于日期、楼层、比赛名次等。

keypoints.title: 按意义选择数词
keypoints.body: 表达数量时用基数词；表达顺序、日期中的“日”、楼层或名次时用序数词。注意整数、分数、小数和百分数的读法，并根据语境确定数词的形式。

exercises.stem: 选择能正确完成句子的选项：The awards ceremony will be held on ___ of June, and the winners will stand on the ___ floor for a group photo.

choices.label: A
choices.text: twenty-first; third

choices.label: B
choices.text: twenty-one; three

choices.label: C
choices.text: twenty-first; three

choices.label: D
choices.text: twenty-one; third

exercises.explanation: 日期中的“日”和楼层都表示顺序，因此要用序数词。21日读作the twenty-first，第三层读作the third floor。

keypoints.title: 核心词汇范围
keypoints.body: 考试大纲词汇（约3500词）是考试要求掌握的核心英语词汇范围，通常包括词形、读音、基本意义、常见词性和主要用法，具体词目以相应大纲为准。

keypoints.title: 分层掌握词汇
keypoints.body: 学习每个词时，应结合语境掌握其常用义、词性变化、固定搭配和基本句型；可按主题、词根词缀或词族归类，并通过阅读、听力和写作反复运用。

exercises.stem: 选择最恰当的词完成句子：Regular reading can ___ students' vocabulary and improve their ability to express ideas.

choices.label: A
choices.text: expand

choices.label: B
choices.text: exchange

choices.label: C
choices.text: examine

choices.label: D
choices.text: escape

exercises.explanation: expand表示“扩大、增加”，expand one's vocabulary是常见搭配，意为“扩大某人的词汇量”。其他选项在意义和搭配上都不符合语境。

keypoints.title: 主题拓展词汇
keypoints.body: 主题相关的扩展词汇是围绕某一主题，在基本词汇之外补充的词语，用于更准确地理解相关语篇、描述具体内容和完成主题表达。其范围会随主题、语篇和学习任务变化。

keypoints.title: 结合主题积累
keypoints.body: 先根据主题和上下文推测词义，再核对词典；同时记录词性、常见搭配和典型语境，并把词汇按主题网络归类，在口头或书面任务中主动使用。

exercises.stem: 在“校园环保”主题语境中阅读短文，推测加粗词的含义：To reduce food waste, the school collects fruit peels and other organic waste. The waste is put into a compost bin, where it slowly turns into nutrient-rich soil that can be used in the school garden. In this context, compost most likely means ____。

choices.label: A
choices.text: 堆肥，即由有机废物制成的肥料

choices.label: B
choices.text: 一种用来盛水的塑料容器

choices.label: C
choices.text: 将食物冷藏保存的方法

choices.label: D
choices.text: 清理操场的工具

exercises.explanation: 上下文提到果皮等有机废物经过处理后变成富含养分、可用于校园花园的土壤，因此compost指“堆肥”，即由有机废物制成的肥料。

keypoints.title: 混合与缩略的含义
keypoints.body: 混合是把两个或多个词的部分拼合成新词，如brunch由breakfast和lunch混合而成；缩略是保留词或短语的部分形式，如ad由advertisement缩略而来，UN由United Nations缩略而来。

keypoints.title: 形式简洁且受语境影响
keypoints.body: 混合词和缩略形式通常比原表达更简洁，常见于日常交流、媒体和专业领域；有些已成为规范词语，有些带有非正式色彩，使用时要根据对象和语境选择。

keypoints.title: 不可随意拆解或替换
keypoints.body: 看到缩略形式时，不能只按字面猜义，也不能把非正式缩略语用于所有场合。要结合上下文确认完整形式、词义和读法，并注意有的缩略语按字母读，有的按单词读。

exercises.stem: 下列关于混合词和缩略形式的判断正确的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: brunch 是由 breakfast 和 lunch 的完整形式直接并列组成的缩写词。

choices.label: B
choices.text: ad 是由 advertisement 和另一个词的部分拼合而成的混合词。

choices.label: C
choices.text: brunch 是 breakfast 和 lunch 的部分拼合形成的混合词；ad 是 advertisement 的缩略形式，正式语境中可根据对象和场合决定是否改用 advertisement。

choices.label: D
choices.text: UN 必须像普通单词一样按一个完整单词读，不能按字母读。

exercises.explanation: brunch 取 breakfast 和 lunch 的部分拼合而成，属于混合词；ad 保留了 advertisement 的部分形式，属于缩略形式。二者都较简洁，但使用时要结合语境，正式场合有时应使用完整表达。UN 通常按字母读作 /ˌjuː ˈen/，不能一概按普通单词处理。

keypoints.title: 合成法的含义
keypoints.body: 合成法是把两个或两个以上的独立词或词根组合起来，构成一个新词的方法。例如，class与room合成classroom，sun与light合成sunlight。

keypoints.title: 识别合成词
keypoints.body: 遇到较长词时，可尝试划分其组成部分，再结合各部分的基本意义和上下文推测整体词义。但合成词的整体意义有时并非各部分意义的简单相加。

exercises.stem: 阅读句子：The children left their backpacks in the classroom. 对 classroom 的构词方式和整体意义理解正确的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: classroom 由独立词 class 和 room 合成，表示用于上课或教学的房间。

choices.label: B
choices.text: classroom 是由 class 的词尾变化形成的，room 不参与构词。

choices.label: C
choices.text: classroom 是 breakfast 和 lunch 一类的混合词。

choices.label: D
choices.text: classroom 中的 room 只表示“一个房间”，所以 classroom 只能指任意房间。

exercises.explanation: class 和 room 都可以独立成词，二者组合构成合成词 classroom，整体表示“教室”，即用于上课或教学的房间。合成词的整体意义应结合组成部分和语境理解，不能只作机械拆分。

keypoints.title: 转化法的含义
keypoints.body: 转化法是在词形和拼写基本不变的情况下，使一个词转作另一种词类，形成新的词义或句法功能。例如，名词email可转作动词，表示“给……发电子邮件”。

keypoints.title: 不要只看词形
keypoints.body: 同一词形在句中充当的词类可能不同，不能仅凭拼写判断词性。应结合其在句中的位置、搭配和意义判断是否发生了转化。

exercises.stem: 在句子“Please email the revised schedule to me tonight.”中，email 的词类和构词现象判断正确的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: email 是名词，因为它表示一种电子信息。

choices.label: B
choices.text: email 在句中作动词，表示“给……发电子邮件”，是名词 email 转化为动词的用法。

choices.label: C
choices.text: email 是形容词，用来修饰 revised schedule。

choices.label: D
choices.text: email 是缩略语，因此在句中不能作谓语。

exercises.explanation: email 位于祈使句中 please 之后，并可带宾语 the revised schedule，表示一个动作，因此在此处是动词，意为“给……发电子邮件”。它的拼写与名词 email 基本不变，只是词类和句法功能发生了变化，体现了转化法。

keypoints.title: 前缀构词的含义
keypoints.body: 前缀构词是在词根或词的前面加上前缀，形成新词。前缀通常改变词义，如un-表示否定，re-表示重复，构成unhappy、rewrite等词。

keypoints.title: 前缀的常见作用
keypoints.body: 前缀构词通常主要改变词义，词性往往保持不变；但具体作用取决于前缀和词根。识别时应同时观察前缀含义、词根意义及新词在语境中的用法。

exercises.stem: 在句子“The team had to rewrite the report because the first version was unclear.”中，下列对 rewrite 的构词分析最准确的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: rewrite 是在 write 后加上后缀 -er 构成的名词，表示“写作者”。

choices.label: B
choices.text: rewrite 是在 write 前加上前缀 re- 构成的动词，re- 表示“再次”，所以 rewrite 表示“重写”。

choices.label: C
choices.text: rewrite 是在 write 前加上前缀 re- 构成的形容词，表示“再次书写的”。

choices.label: D
choices.text: rewrite 是在 write 后加上后缀 -ly 构成的副词，表示“重新地”。

exercises.explanation: rewrite 由前缀 re- 加在动词 write 前构成。re- 常表示“再次”，因此 rewrite 意为“重写”；它仍然是动词，词性没有改变。

keypoints.title: 后缀构词的含义
keypoints.body: 后缀构词是在词根或词的后面加上后缀，形成新词。后缀常改变词义或词性，如teach加-er构成teacher，quick加-ly构成quickly。

keypoints.title: 后缀与词性的关系
keypoints.body: 不同后缀常有较稳定的构词作用：-er常构成表示人的名词，-ful常构成形容词，-ly常构成副词。判断词义时，要结合词根、后缀及具体语境。

exercises.stem: 在句子“The researcher explained the result clearly.”中，下列对 clearly 的构词分析正确的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: clearly 由形容词 clear 加后缀 -ly 构成，-ly 使其成为副词，表示“清楚地”。

choices.label: B
choices.text: clearly 由前缀 re- 加在 clear 前构成，表示“再次清楚”。

choices.label: C
choices.text: clearly 由 clear 加后缀 -er 构成名词，表示“使人清楚的人”。

choices.label: D
choices.text: clearly 由 clear 加后缀 -ful 构成形容词，表示“充满清楚的”。

exercises.explanation: clearly = clear + -ly。clear 是形容词，后缀 -ly 通常把形容词转化为副词，因此 clearly 表示“清楚地”，在句中修饰动词 explained。

keypoints.title: 词族与派生关系是什么
keypoints.body: 词族是由同一词根或基本词通过加前缀、后缀等方式形成的一组词。词族成员在词形、词义上有联系，派生关系体现为一个词由另一个词派生而来。

keypoints.title: 派生词的主要特点
keypoints.body: 派生词常因词缀变化而改变词性或词义，如名词、动词、形容词之间相互派生；有些派生还会引起拼写或读音变化。识别共同词根有助于理解和记忆词义。

exercises.stem: 围绕基本词 help，形成了 help、helpful、helpless、unhelpful、helpfully 等词。下列关于这个词族及其派生关系的说法正确的是（多选）：

choices.label: A
choices.text: helpful 由 help 加后缀 -ful 构成，是形容词。

choices.label: B
choices.text: unhelpful 可看作在 helpful 前加前缀 un- 构成，词性仍为形容词，但意义变为“没有帮助的”。

choices.label: C
choices.text: helpfully 可看作由 helpful 加后缀 -ly 构成，是副词。

choices.label: D
choices.text: helpless 由 help 前加前缀 un- 构成，与 unhelpful 的构词方式相同。

exercises.explanation: 这些词共享基本词 help，词形和词义彼此相关，构成一个词族。helpful 是 help + -ful；unhelpful 是 un- + helpful；helpfully 是 helpful + -ly，且形容词变为副词。helpless 则是 help + -less，不是由 un- 加在 help 前构成的。

keypoints.title: 获取事实性信息是什么
keypoints.body: 获取事实性具体信息是从听到的内容中准确找出明确提及的事实，如人物、时间、地点、数字、事件和具体行为等，并判断其与问题的对应关系。

keypoints.title: 听取具体信息的方法
keypoints.body: 听前先读题并预测所需信息的类型；听时关注关键词、数字、时间和地点等，及时记录；听后结合语境核对答案，注意区分相近信息和干扰信息。

exercises.stem:
听力材料（由教师播放）：Good afternoon, volunteers. This is a reminder about our school clean-up meeting. It was originally planned for Monday at 3:00 p.m., but it has been changed to Tuesday, June 18, at 4:30 p.m. We will meet in Room 204, not in the auditorium. Please bring a pair of gloves and a blue pen.

Question: When and where will the meeting be held?

choices.label: A
choices.text: On Tuesday, June 18, at 4:30 p.m. in Room 204.

choices.label: B
choices.text: On Monday at 3:00 p.m. in the auditorium.

choices.label: C
choices.text: On Tuesday, June 18, at 4:30 p.m. in the auditorium.

choices.label: D
choices.text: On Monday at 4:30 p.m. in Room 204.

exercises.explanation: 录音先提到原定时间是周一下午3点，随后明确说会议改到6月18日星期二下午4点半，并在204室举行，而不是礼堂。因此选A。

keypoints.title: 理解主旨要义是什么
keypoints.body: 理解主旨要义是把握听力语篇或片段的中心话题、主要内容、目的或核心观点，形成对整体意义的概括，而不是只关注零散细节。

keypoints.title: 判断听力主旨的方法
keypoints.body: 结合标题、开头、结尾和反复出现的关键词，关注说话者强调的内容，联系上下文概括整体意思。选择或概括答案时，应以全文信息为依据，避免被单个细节干扰。

exercises.stem:
听力材料（由教师播放）：Many students think that improving vocabulary means memorizing long lists of words. However, a better way is to learn words in context. When you meet a new word in a book or an article, write down the sentence in which it appears and try to use the word in a sentence of your own. You can also review the word later and use it in a conversation or an email. There is no need to learn every meaning of a word at once. The important thing is to understand and use it in real situations.

Question: What is the talk mainly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How to improve vocabulary by learning and using words in context.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Why students should memorize every meaning of a new word.

choices.label: C
choices.text: How to write better emails and have longer conversations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Why reading books is more useful than studying word lists.

exercises.explanation: 全文围绕词汇学习方法展开，重点强调在语境中理解、复习并实际运用词语。B与录音中“没有必要一次学会所有词义”相反，C和D只涉及局部信息，不能概括全文主旨。

keypoints.title: 听力推断是什么
keypoints.body: 对听到的内容作出推断，是根据语篇中明确的信息、上下文、语气和相关背景知识，推测没有直接说出的意义，如说话意图、人物态度、关系或可能结果。

keypoints.title: 听力推断的方法
keypoints.body: 先提取与问题相关的线索，再结合上下文分析线索之间的关系，排除与原文矛盾的选项，得出有依据的结论。推断应以听到的信息为基础，不能仅凭个人猜测。

exercises.stem:
听力材料（由教师播放）：Man: Your train to Bristol leaves at 8:40 from Platform 6. I’m afraid it has been delayed by twenty minutes because of a signal problem.
Woman: Oh no! I have a job interview at ten. Is there another train I can take?
Man: The 8:55 train from Platform 4 goes through Bath. You’ll have to change trains there, but it should get you to Bristol on time.
Woman: Then I’ll take that one. Thank you.

Question: What can be inferred about the woman?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She is worried about being late for an important appointment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She has decided to cancel her job interview.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She prefers to travel through Bath for sightseeing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She does not know how to buy a train ticket.

exercises.explanation: 女子得知原列车晚点后立即说自己十点有面试，并询问替代车次，最后选择需要换乘但能准时到达的列车。这表明她担心因晚点错过重要面试；其他选项与对话信息不符。

keypoints.title: 意图与态度的含义
keypoints.body: 说话者的意图是其希望听者理解、接受或采取行动的目的；态度是其对人、事或观点所持的情感和评价，如赞同、怀疑、关切或不满。

keypoints.title: 从多种线索推断
keypoints.body: 先概括说话内容，再关注请求、建议、评价等表达，结合语气、重音、上下文和说话结果判断意图与态度；遇到暗示时，不只按字面理解。

exercises.stem:
请听下面的对话：
Man: Did you manage to read my proposal for extending the school garden?
Woman: I did. The plan is thoughtful, and I especially like the part about using rainwater. But with exams only three weeks away, asking each class to give up two afternoons may be difficult. Could we start with one trial class and collect evidence first?
Man: So you don't think it will work?
Woman: I think it has promise. I just don't want a good idea to lose support because we rush it.

What is the woman's intention and attitude?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To reject the proposal and ask the man to abandon it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To suggest a smaller trial while expressing cautious support.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To persuade the man to postpone the project until next year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To criticize the use of rainwater and recommend a different plan.

exercises.explanation: 她明确表示方案周全、有前景，说明她总体赞同；同时她担心考试临近、一次投入过大，因此建议先由一个班试行并收集证据。她的意图是提出更稳妥的实施方式，态度是谨慎支持，而不是拒绝。

keypoints.title: 话题转换的含义
keypoints.body: 话题转换是对话从原来讨论的主要对象或问题转向另一个对象或问题。转换后，后续内容通常围绕新的中心展开，而不是仅补充原话题的细节。

keypoints.title: 识别转换信号
keypoints.body: 先抓住当前话题的核心词，留意转折、补充、提问或插入新信息等信号，再判断后续内容是否围绕新的对象展开，并及时更新对话主题。

exercises.stem:
请听下面的对话：
A: Have you found out whether the student center will stay open during the holiday?
B: Yes, until six every weekday. The reading room will close at five, though.
A: That should be enough for my project. Oh, before we talk about the project, I need to ask about the debate team's trip to Nanjing. Has the train booking been confirmed?
B: Not yet. Ms. Lee is waiting for the final list of names.

What is the main topic after the conversation shifts?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The student center's holiday opening hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The reading room's closing time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The debate team's trip and train booking.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The speaker's project schedule.

exercises.explanation: 对话开始围绕学生中心和阅览室的开放时间展开。说话者用“before we talk about the project”引出新的问题，随后连续谈到辩论队去南京的旅行和火车预订，因此后续中心话题已经转换为辩论队出行安排。

keypoints.title: 适应听辨差异
keypoints.body: 应对语速与口音差异，是根据说话快慢和发音特点调整听辨方式，借助语境、重音、关键词及上下文，保持对主要信息的理解。

keypoints.title: 分层处理语音信息
keypoints.body: 语速较快时按意群听，先抓重音和关键词；口音不熟时结合上下文和语境猜测词义，必要时请求重复或确认，不必停留在每个音节上。

keypoints.title: 不要因小失大
keypoints.body: 不要因个别词或音节没听清就停止理解、反复回想；也不要把不熟悉的口音直接判断为错误发音，应先利用整体语境确认意思。

exercises.stem: 你正在听一段校长访谈。校长语速较快，并带有你不熟悉的口音。你只听清了重音词“new schedule”和“Monday”，中间有几个音节没有听清。此时最合适的做法是什么？

choices.label: A
choices.text: 立即停止听后文，反复回想每一个没有听清的音节。

choices.label: B
choices.text: 结合上下文利用重音词推断主要意思；如果关键信息仍不确定，再请求重复或确认。

choices.label: C
choices.text: 认为这是错误发音，忽略包含这些词的句子。

choices.label: D
choices.text: 只根据最后听到的一个词猜测整段话的意思。

exercises.explanation: 面对快语速和不熟悉的口音，应先按意群抓住重音词和关键词，再结合上下文理解主要信息，而不是被个别音节拖住。若日期或安排等关键信息仍不明确，可以请求对方重复或确认。

keypoints.title: 关键词的含义
keypoints.body: 关键词是语句或语篇中承载核心信息、能帮助判断主题和细节的词语，常包括人物、地点、时间、数字、动作、原因和结果等。

keypoints.title: 围绕任务抓重点
keypoints.body: 听前先明确问题或任务，听时重点捕捉反复出现、重读或与任务直接相关的词，并将关键词与上下文联系起来，概括主要信息。

keypoints.title: 不要记录所有词
keypoints.body: 关键词不是所有听到的词，也不一定是最难的词。若试图逐词记录，容易错过后续内容；应优先记录能回答问题的核心信息。

exercises.stem: 你正在听一则校园广播，任务是回答：When and where will the talk be held, and what should students bring? 录音中提到：The talk on ocean pollution, originally planned for Tuesday afternoon, will now be held in Room 204 at 3:30 p.m. on Thursday. Please bring your student ID and a notebook. 听时最值得优先记录哪组信息？

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tuesday afternoon; ocean pollution; talk

choices.label: B
choices.text: Thursday, 3:30 p.m.; Room 204; student ID and notebook

choices.label: C
choices.text: 把录音中的每个词都按顺序记录下来

choices.label: D
choices.text: originally; pollution; planned; held

exercises.explanation: 题目要求关注时间、地点和携带物品，因此应优先记录 Thursday、3:30 p.m.、Room 204、student ID 和 notebook。Tuesday 是被更正的原计划，难词也不一定是关键词；逐词记录还可能影响对后续信息的捕捉。

keypoints.title: 听前预测的含义
keypoints.body: 读题预测听力内容是指在播放录音前，利用题干、选项、图片和已知语境中的关键词，推测录音的主题、人物关系、场景、信息类型及可能出现的答案范围，为听中抓取重点做准备。

keypoints.title: 基于题目逐步预测
keypoints.body: 先看题干，圈出疑问词、时间、地点、人物和数字等线索；再比较选项，判断它们的差异和录音可能考查的信息；最后形成简短预期。录音中要以实际听到的信息为准，发现不符及时调整。

exercises.stem: 录音尚未播放。你先看到以下题目：You will hear a conversation between a hotel guest and a receptionist. Question: What does the guest want to change? A. the check-in date  B. the room type  C. the breakfast time  D. the payment method。哪项是最恰当的听前预测记录？

choices.label: A
choices.text: 场景是酒店，人物是住客与前台；录音可能围绕预订信息中的某一项变更展开，听时要核实具体是哪一项。

choices.label: B
choices.text: 住客一定要改入住日期，因为酒店对话通常先谈日期。

choices.label: C
choices.text: 录音主要会介绍城市天气，四个选项都不必重点关注。

choices.label: D
choices.text: 先把四个选项逐字抄写，听到任何熟悉的词就立即选择对应项。

exercises.explanation: 题干和选项可以帮助判断场景、人物关系及信息类型：这是酒店中的变更请求，重点可能是日期、房型、早餐时间或付款方式中的一项。预测只是听前假设，具体答案仍需以录音为准，不能把某个选项直接当成答案。

keypoints.title: 速记与符号记录含义
keypoints.body: 速记与符号记录是听辨过程中用关键词、缩写、数字、首字母或约定符号快速留下核心信息，并按一定顺序保留信息关系的记录方法，目的是减轻记忆负担，而不是逐字抄录。

keypoints.title: 抓重点快速记录
keypoints.body: 优先记录人名、地点、时间、数量、否定词和转折后的信息；用箭头表示因果或变化，用“+”“−”等表示增减，用缩写代替高频词。符号须保持个人前后一致，听后立即补全不完整信息。

exercises.stem: 录音内容如下：Because the north gate is under repair, the shuttle will not leave from Gate 1 this Friday. Instead, it will leave from Gate 3 at 8:10 a.m. and reach the museum twenty minutes later. The afternoon service remains unchanged.本题约定：−表示不使用或取消，→表示变化或到达，+表示增加或之后。以下哪项速记最能快速、准确地保留核心信息及其关系？

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fri: north gate repair; −G1 → G3, 8:10 a.m. → museum +20m; PM unchanged

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because the north gate is under repair, the shuttle will not leave from Gate 1 this Friday. Instead, it will leave from Gate 3 at 8:10 a.m. and reach the museum twenty minutes later.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Friday, gate 1, gate 3, museum, afternoon

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fri: G1 → museum 8:10; PM changed

exercises.explanation: A用缩写、数字和符号记录了星期、原因、原出发点被取消、改为Gate 3、时间、到达博物馆及晚间班次不变等核心信息，并保留了转折和先后关系。B接近逐字抄录，速度慢；C缺少信息关系；D误记了出发点和下午班次。

keypoints.title: 跨文化文本的含义
keypoints.body: 阅读跨文化题材文本是阅读涉及不同国家、民族或文化群体的故事、说明、对话等语篇，理解其中的事实信息、文化现象、价值观念及其表达方式。

keypoints.title: 把握文化信息
keypoints.body: 先判断文本涉及的文化背景和交际场景，再定位人物行为、习俗、节日、礼仪及观点等信息；结合上下文理解文化含义，区分文本事实与人物立场，不用单一文化标准简单评判差异。

exercises.stem: Read the passage and choose the best answer. At a university welcome dinner in Singapore, Aiko, who had grown up in Japan, received a small notebook from Daniel, a student from Brazil. She smiled, thanked him, and put it in her bag without opening it. Daniel first thought she did not like the gift. Later, Aiko explained that in her family people usually open gifts at home, so that the giver and receiver do not have to compare their reactions in front of others. She also said that many of her friends opened gifts immediately, and she was happy to follow that practice at formal events. What is the best understanding of Aiko’s behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She disliked the gift and tried to hide her reaction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her behavior reflected a family custom and should be understood in its cultural context, not treated as rejection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: People from Japan never open gifts in public.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gifts must always be opened later at formal events.

exercises.explanation: Aiko later explains the reason for her behavior, so it reflects a familiar family custom rather than dislike. The passage also shows that customs vary among people and situations; therefore, her action should not be judged by one fixed cultural standard. C and D use absolute statements unsupported by the text.

keypoints.title: 文学作品阅读的含义
keypoints.body: 阅读文学作品是通过阅读小说、诗歌、戏剧等文学文本，理解情节或意象、人物形象、情感变化和主题思想，并感受语言、结构及表现手法的活动。

keypoints.title: 结合细节品读作品
keypoints.body: 阅读时先梳理事件发展或诗句层次，再结合关键细节分析人物、情感和主题；关注反复、对比、象征、押韵等表达效果，并用文本证据支持理解，不把个人感受替代作品信息。

exercises.stem: Read the passage and choose the best answer. Every morning before school, Lina stopped at an abandoned railway platform and swept one narrow path through the dust. No train had stopped there since her grandfather’s time. Her brother called it a waste of a broom. Lina said nothing; she placed a blue cup on the bench and filled it with water for sparrows. One spring morning, a survey team arrived to inspect the line. They followed the clean path and noticed the cup. The next month, the town repaired the platform and turned it into a park. Lina kept sweeping, even after flowers were planted. When her brother asked why, she replied, ‘Because someone has to begin.’ What does Lina’s repeated act of sweeping mainly reveal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She hopes to find a job on the railway.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her quiet persistence can draw attention to a neglected place and help bring about change.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She believes dust is dangerous for the sparrows.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She knows that the town has already planned to build a park.

exercises.explanation: The empty platform, the clean path, the cup for sparrows, and the later repair of the place show that Lina’s repeated action expresses care and persistence. Her words, ‘Because someone has to begin,’ further support the theme that individual action can start wider change. The other options are not supported by the plot.

keypoints.title: 认识新闻与时评
keypoints.body: 新闻主要客观报道新近发生的事实，时评则围绕新闻事件或社会现象进行分析、评价并表达观点。阅读时要分别把握事实信息、核心观点、论据和作者态度。

keypoints.title: 分清事实与观点
keypoints.body: 先读标题和导语，概括人物、事件、时间、地点及结果；再区分事实陈述与评价性表达，梳理时评的论点和论据，并结合来源与语境判断立场。

exercises.stem: Read the news report and editorial, then choose TWO correct statements. News report: ‘City Library Opens Evening Study Room’ Riverside City Library opened an evening study room on Tuesday in a formerly unused meeting room. According to a library notice, the room will be available from 6 to 9 p.m. on weekdays through June. The library reported that 120 students used it on the first evening. Staff members will collect users’ suggestions before deciding whether to extend the program. Editorial: ‘A Welcome Room, but Not the Final Answer’ The new study room is a sensible response to students who lack a quiet place to work. However, one room cannot meet every student’s needs. The library should publish monthly usage figures and ask students in different neighborhoods for advice before expanding the program. Calling the project a complete success now would be premature. Which TWO statements are correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The news report states that the study room opened on Tuesday.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The phrase ‘a sensible response’ expresses the editorial writer’s evaluation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The library has promised to keep the room open after June.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The editorial presents the project’s complete success as already proven.

exercises.explanation: A is a fact reported in the news text. B is an evaluative expression in the editorial, showing the writer’s judgment. The report says that extension will be considered, not promised, so C is incorrect. The editorial says that calling the project a complete success is premature, so D is incorrect.

keypoints.title: 理解科普说明文本
keypoints.body: 科普与说明类文本以介绍对象、解释现象、阐明原理或说明方法为主要目的，内容强调准确性和条理性，常借助定义、分类、比较、举例和数据等方式展开。

keypoints.title: 把握说明脉络
keypoints.body: 先确定说明对象和说明目的，再梳理段落层次，关注定义、特征、原因、作用及数据等关键信息，借助关联词判断说明顺序，概括文本主要内容。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and choose the best answer.

City trees are often treated as decoration, but they can also be understood as part of a city's cooling infrastructure—natural features that help lower heat in built-up areas. They do this in two main ways. Their leaves block sunlight from reaching roads and walls, while water released from the leaves cools the surrounding air.

This effect is not identical everywhere. In a summer comparison of six similar streets, those with continuous tree cover were 4 to 7°C cooler at midday than streets with very little cover. The difference was greatest where trees shaded large areas of pavement.

However, planting trees does not automatically solve urban heat. Young trees provide little shade, and trees planted in dry or crowded spaces may grow poorly. Cities therefore need to choose suitable species and provide enough room and water. Which option best describes how the passage is organized?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It tells the history of city tree planting and then predicts how it will change in the future.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It compares two kinds of trees and argues that one kind should replace the other.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It defines a function of city trees, explains how that function works, presents comparative data, and then discusses conditions for achieving the effect.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It lists several problems caused by trees and finally suggests removing them from crowded cities.

exercises.explanation: 文章先把城市树木界定为能够降温的“cooling infrastructure”，接着用“two main ways”解释树木通过遮阴和蒸腾作用降温，再用街道温度对比数据提供证据，最后用“However”说明树木降温受树龄、空间和水分等条件限制，并提出管理要求。因此，C准确概括了说明对象、说明脉络和说明方法。

keypoints.title: 判断作者立场
keypoints.body: 判断作者观点与态度，是依据文本中的主旨、论据、评价性词语和表达语气，确定作者对人、事或现象的看法、立场及情感倾向，而不是代入个人意见。

keypoints.title: 寻找态度线索
keypoints.body: 重点关注标题、首尾段、转折和总结句，以及褒贬词、情态词和反问句；同时区分作者观点与引用人物的观点，结合全文证据判断态度的方向和强弱。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and choose the best answer.

Let the App Suggest, Not Decide

Many schools are testing AI apps that give students instant feedback on drafts. Supporters call them patient second readers; critics warn that the apps may reward formulaic writing and misunderstand unusual ideas. One critic says, ‘A machine cannot recognize a truly original voice.’ That warning deserves attention, but it does not settle the issue.

In fact, an app can quickly point out repeated words, missing transitions, or sentences likely to confuse a reader. This can leave teachers more time to discuss evidence and purpose. Yet the feedback is based on patterns in data, so it may favor familiar styles. A student should never be told that a creative sentence is wrong simply because an algorithm finds it unusual.

AI writing tools, then, are useful assistants rather than judges. Schools should teach students to question their suggestions and keep teachers responsible for final decisions. Used in this limited way, the apps can support writing instruction without replacing human judgment.

What is the author's attitude toward AI writing-feedback apps?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Completely opposed, because machines can never contribute to writing instruction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Uncritically enthusiastic, because the apps are more reliable than teachers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cautiously supportive, while insisting that the apps have limits and must not replace human judgment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Indifferent, because the use of such apps has no meaningful effect on education.

exercises.explanation: 作者承认应用程序能发现重复用词、衔接缺失等问题，说明其具有辅助价值；同时用“may favor familiar styles”和“should never be told”等表达指出算法的局限。结尾将其定位为“useful assistants rather than judges”，并要求教师保留最终决定权，表明作者是有条件地支持，而非盲目赞成。文中的批评意见属于被引用者的观点，不等同于作者立场。

keypoints.title: 语境推断词义
keypoints.body: 根据上下文推断词义，是利用词语所在的句子、段落、篇章语境，并结合构词形式和已有知识，推测其在当前语境中的恰当含义，而非机械套用词典释义。

keypoints.title: 多线索验证词义
keypoints.body: 先判断词语的词性和句中作用，再查找定义、举例、同义、反义、因果或转折等线索；将推测义代入原句和上下文检验，确保语意连贯。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and choose the best answer.

When heavy rain falls, streets and roofs can send a large amount of water into a river within a short time. A wetland beside the river can act as a buffer between the river and nearby houses. Its shallow pools and water-loving plants hold back some of the extra water and release it slowly. As a result, the river rises less suddenly, giving communities more time to respond. Without this natural buffer, much of the water might move downstream at once.

What does the word ‘buffer’ most nearly mean in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A protective system that softens or reduces the effect of a problem.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A narrow channel that carries water away as quickly as possible.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A device used to measure the amount of rain in an area.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A source of polluted water located near a river.

exercises.explanation: “Buffer”在句中作名词，位于河流和房屋之间。后文说明湿地先蓄住部分雨水，再缓慢释放，使河水上涨不那么突然，并给社区更多应对时间。因此该词在这里指能够缓冲、减轻洪水影响的保护性系统，A最符合上下文。

keypoints.title: 明确获取细节信息
keypoints.body: 理解具体信息是从语篇中准确获取明确表达的事实、细节和局部关系，如人物、时间、地点、原因、结果、数量或行为等，并结合语境理解其同义改写。

keypoints.title: 定位并核对信息
keypoints.body: 先根据题干确定信息类别和关键词，再在语篇中快速定位相关句段；注意同义替换、代词指代和否定表达，最后结合上下文核对信息是否完整、准确。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Every Saturday morning from 9:00 to 11:00, the Riverside High eco-club opens a Repair Corner in an unused classroom. Local residents can bring small household items, such as lamps, bags, and bicycle parts. The volunteers do not simply take the items away; they first examine them with the owners and explain the problem. Then they show the owners how to repair the items when possible. During the first month, 38 residents visited the Repair Corner. On the second Saturday, retired engineer Mr. Patel joined the volunteers after he saw the club's notice at a bus stop. He later showed several students how to repair a loose bicycle brake.
Why did Mr. Patel join the Repair Corner?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He wanted to buy a new bicycle.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He noticed information about the activity at a bus stop.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He was invited by a student from the eco-club.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He needed to borrow some tools from the school.

exercises.explanation: 文中明确说 Mr. Patel joined the volunteers after he saw the club's notice at a bus stop，因此 B 正确。其他选项在语篇中没有依据。

keypoints.title: 辨明事实和观点
keypoints.body: 事实是能够通过语篇内容、客观资料或证据加以验证的信息；观点是说话者或作者对事物的判断、评价、态度、推测或主张，带有一定主观性。

keypoints.title: 依据证据判断性质
keypoints.body: 先看句子是否陈述可核实的事件、数据或情况，再观察是否含有评价性词语、情感态度、推测和建议。不能仅凭句式判断，还要结合上下文和语篇证据。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question.
In May, the city introduced an electric shuttle between the railway station and the central market. The shuttle runs from 6:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. and stops at three places. According to a report from the transport office, its average daily ridership rose from 410 in May to 560 in August. The local newspaper's editor called the shuttle the smartest transport decision in years. Some shop owners also said that more customers had visited their stores since the service began.
Which of the following is an opinion rather than a fact?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The shuttle began service in May.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The shuttle stops at three places.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its average daily ridership rose from 410 to 560.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The shuttle is the smartest transport decision in years.

exercises.explanation: A、B、C分别涉及开始时间、停靠数量和可查证的数据，属于事实。D中的 smartest 是带有评价色彩的最高级判断，表达了编辑的主观看法，因此是观点。

keypoints.title: 读出言外之意
keypoints.body: 推断隐含意义与作者意图，是依据语篇中的词句、情节、逻辑关系和语境线索，合理推知未直接说明的信息，以及作者写作的目的、态度或立场。

keypoints.title: 由线索合理推断
keypoints.body: 先找与问题相关的明确线索，再联系前后文、语篇结构和常识进行推理；选择能被多处信息支持的结论，区分文本依据与个人猜想。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question.
When a small book shelf appeared under the roof of the central station, some commuters predicted that nobody would use it. One rainy day, volunteers found several books wet, so they moved the shelf farther under the roof and added a card saying, Take a book, return it, or leave another. Six months later, the shelf was emptied and refilled several times a day. Commuters also left notes recommending books to one another. Lena, the project coordinator, said, We did not create readers; we gave an existing interest a place to be seen.
What is the author's main purpose in writing this passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To explain how volunteers can protect books from rain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To show that a convenient shared space can support people's existing interest in reading.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To prove that commuters prefer printed books to electronic books.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To compare the reading habits of different groups of commuters.

exercises.explanation: 书架被频繁取放、读者留下推荐，且协调人说他们并非创造读者，而是提供了展示兴趣的场所。作者借此说明便利的共享空间能够支持人们原有的阅读兴趣，因此 B 最符合作者意图。

keypoints.title: 把握全文核心
keypoints.body: 理解主旨与要义，是概括语篇围绕的核心对象、主要内容和中心意思，明确作者重点说明、讲述或强调什么，而不是只复述某个细节或照搬标题。

keypoints.title: 整合关键信息
keypoints.body: 先确定语篇讨论的对象和范围，再关注反复出现的信息、段落重点及开头结尾，概括各部分的共同指向；用简洁完整的语句表达中心意思。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and choose the best statement of its main idea.

Every year, many useful objects are thrown away simply because they have a small problem. Repair cafés offer a different response. At regular neighborhood gatherings, volunteers help visitors mend lamps, clothes, toys, and other household items. Visitors do not just receive a service; they watch, ask questions, and often learn to repair things themselves. These events therefore do more than keep objects out of rubbish bins. They bring people together and encourage a habit of using things for longer. Repair cafés cannot replace manufacturers or solve all waste problems, but they show how shared skills can turn an everyday habit into a more sustainable one.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most household objects can be repaired by volunteers in one afternoon.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repair cafés reduce waste while building community and encouraging people to repair and reuse objects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: People should never buy new household goods because repair cafés can solve all waste problems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Manufacturers are mainly responsible for the waste produced by households.

exercises.explanation: 全文围绕 repair cafés 展开，先说明其帮助修理物品，再强调它们通过共享技能减少浪费、增进邻里交流并培养延长物品使用寿命的习惯。B概括了对象、主要内容和中心意义；A只涉及一个细节，C和D则超出或曲解了原文。

keypoints.title: 篇章结构与句间关系
keypoints.body: 篇章结构是语篇各部分的组织方式，如总分、因果、对比、递进等；句间关系是相邻或相近句子在意义和逻辑上的联系。理解二者要把握语篇层次、段落功能及信息推进。

keypoints.title: 识别结构与关系
keypoints.body: 先概括各段和关键句的主要内容，再关注转折、因果、递进等连接词，以及代词、同义词和重复表达，判断句子之间的逻辑关系，最后结合全文主题验证判断。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and choose the best description of its organization.

[1] Many students think that speaking practice requires a special language club.
[2] In fact, ordinary classroom routines can create frequent chances to speak.
[3] For example, students can explain a solution to a partner before writing it down.
[4] They can also summarize a short text for a classmate who was absent.
[5] These activities take only a few minutes, but they make speaking purposeful and regular.
[6] Therefore, the key is not finding a perfect place to speak, but building small speaking tasks into daily learning.

choices.label: A
choices.text: It presents a common belief, corrects it, gives two examples, explains their value, and ends with a conclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It describes the history of speaking clubs, compares two clubs, and rejects both of them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It raises a problem, lists several causes of the problem, and reports the results of an experiment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It states a conclusion first, gives evidence against it, and finally changes to an unrelated topic.

exercises.explanation: 第1句提出学生的常见看法，第2句用 In fact 转折并修正这一看法；第3、4句由 For example 引出两个具体做法，第5句说明这些做法的作用，第6句由 Therefore 总结中心观点。因此篇章是“常见看法—纠正—举例说明—总结”的推进结构。

keypoints.title: 精读与批判性阅读
keypoints.body: 精读是对语篇的词句、段落、结构和细节进行深入理解；批判性阅读是在理解基础上分析作者观点、论据和表达目的，并依据文本证据作出有理有据的判断。

keypoints.title: 深入理解并评价
keypoints.body: 精读时标出关键词句，梳理结构并推断隐含信息；批判性阅读时区分事实与观点，检查论据是否充分、推理是否合理，必要时比较不同观点，再形成自己的结论。

exercises.stem:
Read the passage and choose the best evaluation of the writer's conclusion.

A school newsletter states: “Tablets should replace printed textbooks in every secondary school. In a two-week trial at Green Valley School, 18 of 25 students said that reading on tablets was more interesting. The newsletter concludes that tablets guarantee better learning. However, it does not report whether students' test results changed, nor does it discuss possible screen distraction, cost, or access to charging. The trial involved only one school.”

choices.label: A
choices.text: The conclusion is fully reliable because most of the students preferred reading on tablets.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The evidence suggests that tablets may increase interest for some students, but it is not enough to prove better learning or support their use in every school.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Printed textbooks are always more effective because the trial lasted only two weeks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The trial proves that tablets will improve students' learning in the long term.

exercises.explanation: 18名学生表示阅读更有趣，只能说明这一所学校的部分学生在短期内有较高兴趣，并不能直接证明学习效果更好。该试验时间短、样本和学校范围有限，而且没有提供测试成绩，也未讨论分心、成本和充电条件。因此作者把有限证据推广为“保证更好学习、适用于每所学校”，推理并不充分，B的评价最符合文本证据。

keypoints.title: 语篇填空解题思路
keypoints.body: 七选五等语篇填空是根据全文主题、篇章结构、上下文语义、衔接照应和语言形式，将选项与空缺位置匹配，使语篇内容连贯、结构完整、表达准确。

keypoints.title: 按线索逐步匹配
keypoints.body: 先通读全文，概括主题和结构；再判断空格在段落中的功能，结合前后句、连接词、代词指代和词语复现筛选选项；完成后通读检查逻辑、衔接和语法。

keypoints.title: 避免只看局部
keypoints.body: 不要只依据空格前后的一句话作答，也不要因选项含有相同词语就直接匹配。还要检查选项与全文主题、段落位置、指代对象及逻辑关系是否一致。

exercises.stem:
阅读下面语段，从所给选项中选出最适合填入横线处的一项。

People often believe that protecting the environment requires dramatic changes. In fact, ordinary choices can also make a difference. ________ For instance, bringing a reusable bottle, avoiding unnecessary printing, and choosing public transport can reduce waste and emissions. Such habits may seem too small to matter, but their effect grows when many people repeat them.

choices.label: A
choices.text: What matters is not that each action is dramatic, but that it is repeated and shared.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Environmental problems are caused only by factories in distant cities.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public transport is always the fastest way to travel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some people collect bottles as a hobby.

exercises.explanation: 全文主题是普通环保行为的意义。横线前先提出普通选择也能产生影响，横线后用“For instance”列举具体做法，并用“Such habits”回指这些做法。A概括了环保行动需要重复并由更多人参与，既承接上文，又能引出下文例子。其他选项或偏离主题，或与上下文逻辑不符。解题时不能只看空格前一句，还要结合全文主题、段落推进和指代关系判断。

keypoints.title: 长难句分析
keypoints.body: 长难句通常包含多个分句、从句、非谓语结构或较长修饰成分。分析长难句就是辨认句子主干和层次，理清修饰、指代及分句关系，从而准确理解句意。

keypoints.title: 拆分句子层次
keypoints.body: 先找谓语动词和连接词，确定主句与从句；再标出非谓语、介词短语和定语等修饰成分，划分意群，明确指代关系，最后按逻辑顺序整合句意。

exercises.stem:
阅读下面的长难句，选出对其结构和句意分析最准确的一项。

Although the community garden, which was created by local residents who wanted to make fresh food available to every family, requires regular care, it has brought neighbors together in ways that its founders never expected.

choices.label: A
choices.text: 主句是“it has brought neighbors together...”；Although引导让步状语从句，其中which...修饰community garden，who...修饰residents，that...修饰ways；it指community garden。

choices.label: B
choices.text: 主句是“the community garden requires regular care”；it引导结果状语从句，which修饰care。

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although引导原因状语从句；who修饰community garden；that引导宾语从句，说明founders期待的内容。

choices.label: D
choices.text: 主句由“which was created...”构成；requires和has brought是主句的两个并列谓语，that从句修饰founders。

exercises.explanation: 先找连接词和谓语：Although引导让步状语从句，核心为“the community garden requires regular care”；主句为“it has brought neighbors together...”。which引导非限制性定语从句修饰community garden，who引导定语从句修饰residents，that引导定语从句修饰ways。主句中的it指前面的community garden。按主干、从句和修饰成分分层后，句意是：尽管这个由希望让每个家庭都能获得新鲜食物的当地居民创建的社区花园需要经常照料，但它以创建者未曾预料的方式使邻居们走到了一起。

keypoints.title: 扫读的含义
keypoints.body: 扫读是为寻找特定信息而快速浏览语篇，借助标题、段落、关键词、数字或专名等线索定位内容，不必逐词理解全文。

keypoints.title: 扫读查找步骤
keypoints.body: 先明确查找目标，预测信息可能的形式和位置；再快速浏览并锁定关键词，找到相关段落后回读上下文，核对信息是否准确。

exercises.stem:
阅读下面的通知，回答问题。

Green Skills Week at Riverside Library
The library will offer three free workshops in May. On Monday, May 12, from 4:00 to 5:30 p.m., Maya Chen will teach clothing repair in Room 2. On Tuesday, May 13, bicycle maintenance will be held in the courtyard from 4:30 to 6:00 p.m.; participants should bring a bicycle. On Saturday, May 17, the book-binding workshop will take place in Room 1 from 10:00 to 11:30 a.m. Registration closes two days before each workshop, and places are limited to 20.

A student wants to attend the bicycle-maintenance workshop. Which information is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monday, May 12, in Room 2, from 4:00 to 5:30 p.m.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tuesday, May 13, in the courtyard, from 4:30 to 6:00 p.m.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Saturday, May 17, in the courtyard, from 10:00 to 11:30 a.m.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tuesday, May 13, in Room 1, from 4:00 to 5:30 p.m.

exercises.explanation: 先明确查找目标是“bicycle-maintenance workshop”，再在通知中快速定位含有该关键词的句子。该句明确给出日期为Tuesday, May 13，地点为the courtyard，时间为4:30 to 6:00 p.m.，因此B正确。其他选项混入了服装修补或装订工作坊的日期、地点和时间。

keypoints.title: 略读的含义
keypoints.body: 略读是快速浏览语篇的标题、段落结构、首尾句和关键词，抓住主题与主要内容，暂时忽略次要细节和个别生词。

keypoints.title: 略读把握大意
keypoints.body: 先看标题并预测主题，再关注首段、各段关键句和结尾，留意反复出现的词语，最后用一句话概括全文大意并检查是否完整。

exercises.stem:
请运用略读策略，先关注标题、各段关键句以及反复出现的词语，再选择最能概括全文大意的一项。

Small Changes, Shared Streets

In many cities, streets are designed mainly for cars. As a result, traffic is slow, air is polluted, and neighbors have fewer chances to meet. City planners and residents are therefore looking for ways to make ordinary streets more pleasant.

One idea is the slow street. On selected roads, cars must travel slowly or are limited at certain times. Benches, trees, and small public activities give people reasons to walk, cycle, and talk. In several neighborhoods, local shops have also gained more visitors because people stay longer.

Slow streets are not a complete answer. Cities still need reliable public transport, safe crossings, and careful parking plans. Even so, these projects show that changing shared streets, especially with residents' participation, can improve everyday urban life.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community-based changes to streets can improve urban life, although they need to be part of wider planning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Slow streets mainly help local shops attract more visitors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Traffic pollution is caused by city residents' lack of public transport.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The best way to improve cities is to ban cars on all roads.

exercises.explanation: 标题中的 shared streets 和文中反复出现的 streets、cities、residents 等词提示文章关注城市公共街道的改善。第一段说明问题，第二段介绍 slow streets 的作用，第三段指出其局限并总结居民参与和整体规划的重要性。因此 A 同时概括了措施、作用和限制；B 只涉及局部细节，C 与原文不符，D 夸大了文章观点。

keypoints.title: 讨论与协商
keypoints.body: 参与讨论与协商是围绕共同话题表达观点、倾听和回应他人，通过提问、解释、比较和适当让步，逐步形成共识或作出决定。

keypoints.title: 参与互动步骤
keypoints.body: 先清楚表达观点和理由，主动邀请他人发言；认真倾听并回应，礼貌表示赞同或异议，提出可行方案，比较意见后协商确定结果。

exercises.stem: 英语社团正在协商周末环保活动的时间。Ben 说：I think Sunday afternoon is best because most members are free. Mei 说：I prefer Saturday morning because I have family plans on Sunday. 哪一句话最能推动讨论并帮助大家作出决定？

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sunday is obviously better. We should stop discussing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I agree with Ben, and Mei's plan is not practical.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I lean toward Sunday afternoon because it may suit more members, but I understand Mei's family plans. Could we check everyone's availability first? If many cannot attend on Sunday, Saturday afternoon may be a fair compromise. What do you think?

choices.label: D
choices.text: I don't have a preference, so decide yourselves.

exercises.explanation: C 先表达自己的倾向及理由，再理解并回应 Mei 的困难，随后提出核实成员时间和采用折中方案的可行建议，最后邀请他人继续发表意见，体现了比较、适当让步和协商。A、B 直接否定或终止讨论，D 没有参与协商。

keypoints.title: 发起维持交谈
keypoints.body: 发起与维持交谈是主动开启对话，并通过回应、追问、补充、转换或延续话题等方式保持交流，使交谈自然进行。

keypoints.title: 保持交谈方法
keypoints.body: 可用问候、提问或评论开启话题；交谈中及时回应，使用追问和补充拓展内容，注意轮流发言，必要时用换说法澄清，最后自然结束。

exercises.stem: 你在学校迎接一名刚到校的交换生。以下哪一句最能自然地发起并维持交谈？

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hi. What's your name?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hi, I'm Li Hua. I heard you enjoy photography. What do you like taking pictures of, and how did you get interested in it?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The library is over there. Goodbye.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I like photography.

exercises.explanation: B 先用问候和自我介绍开启交谈，再以共同兴趣作评论，并通过两个开放性问题引导对方补充信息，能够自然延续话题。A 只能完成简单开场，C 直接结束交谈，D 没有回应或提问，难以维持交流。

keypoints.title: 礼貌中断并确认信息
keypoints.body: 得体地打断与澄清，是在口语交流中用礼貌方式请求暂停或发言，并通过重复、换说或提问确认信息，以消除误解、保证交流顺利进行。

keypoints.title: 四步完成打断澄清
keypoints.body: 先用“Excuse me”或“Sorry to interrupt”礼貌引起注意；选择合适停顿提出问题；说明没有听清或没有理解之处；用“Do you mean...?”复述确认，并致谢。

exercises.stem: 在英语小组讨论中，同伴说：“The rehearsal will be in the library at four.”你没有听清是哪一天。下列哪一项回应最得体、最有助于澄清信息？

choices.label: A
choices.text: What? Say it again.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sorry to interrupt. I didn't catch the day. Do you mean the rehearsal is in the library on Thursday at four? Thanks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I disagree. The rehearsal is at five.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep talking. I'll guess the day and time.

exercises.explanation: B先用“Sorry to interrupt”礼貌打断，说明没有听清的内容，再用“Do you mean...?”复述并确认具体信息，最后致谢，符合得体打断与澄清的步骤。A语气生硬，C没有依据且未澄清，D可能造成误解。

keypoints.title: 应对交流障碍的策略
keypoints.body: 交际中的补救策略，是在词语不会、表达受阻、没有听懂或发生误解时，借助替换、解释、询问、重复、确认或非语言手段维持并修复交流。

keypoints.title: 灵活修复交流
keypoints.body: 遇到障碍时先判断问题，再用已知词语换说或描述；可请求对方重复、放慢语速或解释，也可借助手势和示例；表达后确认对方是否理解，避免直接放弃交流。

exercises.stem: 在英语讨论中，你想介绍一种“可堆肥的”包装，但一时想不起“compostable”这个词。下列哪种说法最能运用交际补救策略，维持交流并确认对方是否理解？

choices.label: A
choices.text: I can't say it in English, so let's stop talking about it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I'm not sure of the exact word, but it means something that can break down naturally, like food waste. Does that make sense?

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a kind of package. You should know what I mean.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Please wait. I will look up every word before I continue.

exercises.explanation: B没有因想不起词语而放弃交流，而是先说明困难，再用已知词语解释概念，并询问对方是否理解。这同时运用了替换或描述、解释和确认等补救策略。A直接放弃，C表达不清且语气不当，D不能及时维持口头交流。

keypoints.title: 有依据地阐明观点
keypoints.body: 表达并论证观点，是明确提出对某一问题的看法，并用相关、充分的理由、事实或例子支持观点，必要时回应不同意见，使表达具有说服力。

keypoints.title: 按逻辑组织论证
keypoints.body: 先清楚表明观点，再说明理由并补充事实或例子；可用“because”“for example”“however”等衔接语回应不同看法，最后概括结论。论据应与观点相关且可信。

exercises.stem: 学校正在讨论是否应每周安排一次固定的课外阅读时间。下列哪一段发言最能清楚表达观点并用相关理由、例子和回应不同意见来论证？

choices.label: A
choices.text: I think schools should have a reading period. It is a good idea because I like reading.

choices.label: B
choices.text: I believe schools should offer a weekly reading period because it can help students develop a regular reading habit and relax. For example, students could read books related to their interests for 30 minutes each Friday. Some may say it takes time from other subjects; however, a short fixed period can be planned without replacing core lessons. Therefore, a weekly reading period is worthwhile.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schools should offer it, and our basketball team won its last game. That is why reading time is necessary.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reading may be useful, but schools should do what they want. I have no clear opinion.

exercises.explanation: B先明确提出支持每周阅读时间的观点，接着用培养阅读习惯和放松身心作理由，以每周五阅读30分钟为例，并用“Some may say... however...”回应可能的反对意见，最后概括结论。其论据与观点相关，结构完整，具有较强说服力。

keypoints.title: 面向听众的连续表达
keypoints.body: 口头报告与演讲，是围绕明确主题，面向听众进行有准备、有组织的连续口头表达。报告侧重介绍和说明，演讲还常承担说服、倡议或激励作用。

keypoints.title: 准备并完成口头表达
keypoints.body: 根据目的和听众确定主题，安排开头、主体和结尾；准备关键词、例证或图表，避免照稿朗读；表达时注意发音、语速、停顿、目光和手势，并通过排练及时调整。

exercises.stem: 你将在英语课上面向全班同学进行一次3分钟的演讲，主题是倡议同学减少一次性塑料制品的使用。下列准备和表达方式最符合口头报告与演讲的要求的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: 写出一篇完整稿件，演讲时逐字朗读，不安排排练，以免遗漏内容。

choices.label: B
choices.text: 先根据倡议目的和同学这一听众确定内容，安排开头、主体和结尾，准备关键词及一个具体例子，排练后根据效果调整语速，并注意目光交流和停顿。

choices.label: C
choices.text: 搜集尽可能多的数据，按资料顺序全部读出，不必考虑开头、结尾和听众反应。

choices.label: D
choices.text: 只背诵几个有感染力的句子，现场想到什么就说什么，以体现表达的自然性。

exercises.explanation: 演讲具有说服、倡议或激励作用，需要围绕明确目的和听众组织内容，形成开头、主体、结尾，并借助关键词和例证进行较自然的连续表达。排练有助于调整语速、停顿和表达效果，目光交流也能增强与听众的联系。A、C、D分别存在照稿朗读、缺少组织和准备不足等问题。

keypoints.title: 朗读与复述的含义
keypoints.body: 朗读是把书面语篇清晰、准确、流畅地读出来；复述是在理解内容的基础上，用自己的话按一定顺序重新讲述主要信息。

keypoints.title: 先理解再表达
keypoints.body: 朗读前先弄清词句和语篇结构，注意语音、重音、节奏和停顿；复述时抓住人物、事件、原因和结果，借助提纲按顺序表达，不必逐句背诵。

exercises.stem: 英语课上，学生需要先朗读一篇短文，再在不看原文的情况下复述。下列做法最符合朗读与复述的要求的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: 先弄清生词、句意和短文结构；朗读时按意群处理重音、节奏和停顿；复述时列出人物、事件、原因和结果，用自己的话按顺序表达。

choices.label: B
choices.text: 朗读前不必理解内容，只要尽量读快；复述时逐句背诵原文，确保每个词都不改变。

choices.label: C
choices.text: 朗读时只注意单词发音，不必关注句子之间的关系；复述时只说自己印象最深的一处细节。

choices.label: D
choices.text: 朗读时把每个句子都读成相同的语调；复述时按照想到的内容随意调整顺序，不必说明原因和结果。

exercises.explanation: 朗读要求先理解词句和语篇结构，并通过正确的语音、重音、节奏和停顿清晰流畅地表达。复述则要抓住人物、事件、原因和结果，借助提纲按顺序用自己的话重新讲述，而不是逐句背诵或只复述零散细节。

keypoints.title: 连贯陈述的含义
keypoints.body: 就特定话题连贯陈述，是围绕明确主题，连续表达事实、观点或经历，使内容完整、层次清楚，句子之间具有合乎逻辑的衔接。

keypoints.title: 按结构组织表达
keypoints.body: 先明确话题和表达目的，再列出要点，按照总述—分述、时间顺序或因果关系组织内容；用恰当的连接词衔接，并根据听者反馈调整语速和表达。

exercises.stem: 你要用英语就学生养成每日阅读习惯的好处作一段约两分钟的连贯陈述。下列组织方式最恰当的是：

choices.label: A
choices.text: 先讲一个与阅读无关的旅游故事，再突然列出几个生词，接着重复开头故事，最后用一句随意的话结束。

choices.label: B
